data.title: Wake-up call! Forward Kristensen's double rocks rotated Thailand
data.description: Thailand's preparations for the Fifa Asean Cup final suffered a jolt on Friday night, when a heavily rotated side lost 2-1 to the Philippines in their final Group B fixture at Si Jalak Harupat Stadium in Bandung.

data.title: Phuket festival to draw 140k locals
data.description: PHUKET: The annual nine-day Vegetarian Festival is expected to attract about 140,000 local tourists and generate more than 1.3 billion baht in local spending, the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) says.

data.title: Rider accused of B3.7m theft
data.description: PHUKET: Police have arrested a food delivery rider accused of stealing cash and camera equipment worth more than 3.69 million baht from two foreign residents' homes in Muang district.

data.title: Another slice of history for teen Thai skater Hiro
data.description: Hiro Kaewtathip made history again by winning Thailand's first-ever gold medal at the ISU Figure Skating Junior Grand Prix.

data.title: Star Puripol crowned the Asiad MVP
data.description: Star sprinter Puripol Boonson has been selected by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) as the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the 20th Asian Games after delivering a spectacular performance on the track in Japan.

data.title: Floods won't disrupt IMF meetings, ministry says
data.description: Flooding will not disrupt the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Group in Bangkok on Oct 12-18, and evacuation plans are ready if water levels rise, the Finance Ministry says.

data.title: BMA dropped ball on floods: Uni
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) failed to respond to advance warnings of a potential flood crisis, climate expert Assoc Prof Seree Supratid said.

data.title: Media urges safeguards for Thai PBS
data.description: Six media organisations have called for legal and financial safeguards to protect Thai Public Broadcasting Service (Thai PBS) independence after a Bhumjaithai Party bill proposed changing its funding to annual state budget allocations.

data.title: Suphajee keeps eye on traders
data.description: Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun has ordered strict price checks and stock monitoring to prevent traders from exploiting consumers affected by flooding.

data.title: Call for better teen parent support
data.description: The government must redesign support systems for teenage parents, addressing gaps in welfare, healthcare and laws to tackle complex problems they may face, the Sexualities Studies Association says.

data.title: Currency shifts boost tourism in the South
data.description: A stronger Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar are boosting tourism in Hat Yai and Dan Nok in Songkhla province, with Chinese tourists based in Malaysia among high-spending visitors.

data.title: Govt, BMA under fire for response
data.description: The Bangkok floods have exposed failures in preparedness, warning systems and coordination, with analysts pointing to deeper structural weaknesses in crisis management.

data.title: Govt urges 60/40 co-payment sign-ups before deadline
data.description: More than 22.3 million beneficiaries have confirmed their eligibility for the government's expanded Thais Help Thais Plus (60/40) co-payment scheme, and the government is urging those who have yet to register to do so before the Oct 15 deadline.

data.title: Flood, disaster response 'weak'
data.description: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has proposed structural reforms to the water management system, including unified flood command and proactive disaster funding.

data.title: Govt plays down cost of floods
data.description: The Finance Ministry estimates the floods will have an impact of less than 0.1% on the overall economy, maintaining its forecast of 2-2.5% GDP growth for 2026.

data.title: Israel targets top Hamas leader in deadly Gaza strike on anniversary
data.description: GAZA CITY (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Israel said on Saturday that it attempted to kill Hamas's top leader in the Gaza Strip in an airstrike on an apartment that local officials said killed five people, four of them women.

data.title: Houthis say Saudi Arabia launches dozens of strikes on Yemen capital
data.description: SANAA - Yemen's Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of launching dozens of strikes on Sanaa on Saturday, while an AFP journalist in Riyadh reported seeing flames and smoke coming from an oil facility on the outskirts of the Saudi capital.

data.title: UAE: flydubai co-pilot was planning ‘terrorist act’
data.description: DUBAI - Investigators in the United Arab Emirates have said the co-pilot of a flydubai flight to Israel this week was planning a “terrorist act” and used the cockpit’s emergency axe to attack the captain, but they did not reveal his motive.

data.title: Russia warns diplomats to leave Kyiv before ‘massive’ strikes
data.description: KYIV - Russia on Saturday issued a new call for diplomats and foreigners to leave Kyiv, warning the Ukrainian capital of new “massive” air attacks hours after striking another major bridge in the city.

data.title: Memorable Thai performance yields 18 gold medals
data.description: Taekwondo star Banlung Tubtimdang, sailor Pinchanok Klaysomboon and jiu-jitsu fighter Orapa Senatham each stood atop the podium on Saturday, powering Thailand’s gold medal haul to 18 on the penultimate day of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.

data.title: Flood-battered Bangkok amusement park won’t rule out sale
data.description: The management of Siam Amazing Park is desperately seeking a way to keep the 46-year-old amusement and water park operating after flooding in Bangkok damaged nearly the entire complex, with a sale for 10 billion baht one of many options.

data.title: ONE Championship: Shamil Erdogan demands title shot, calls out retired Anatoly Malykhin
data.description: Shamil Erdogan challenged Anatoly Malykhin to come out of retirement after strengthening his claim to ONE Championship’s vacant heavyweight MMA title with a second-round submission of Paul Elliott.

data.title: Flooding persists in 26 provinces and Bangkok
data.description: Flooding persists in 26 provinces and Bangkok, affecting nearly 1.2 million households and 3.2 million people, the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM) said on Saturday.

data.title: Bulgarian tsar returns ‘home’ after 1,000 years
data.description: SOFIA, Bulgaria - More than 1,000 years after his death, the remains of what may be Tsar Samuel, one of the last major rulers of the First Bulgarian Empire, are returning “home” on Saturday.

data.title: India beat Pakistan in cricket blockbuster
data.description: NAGOYA, Japan - India beat arch-rivals Pakistan to win Asian Games gold on Saturday in a blockbuster cricket final as South Korea’s Tom Kim clinched the men’s golf crown — and will avoid military service.

data.title: Philippines voices concern over Myanmar airstrike deaths
data.description: MANILA - ⁠The ⁠Philippines has expressed concern over ​an airstrike in ‌Myanmar that caused about 50 civilian deaths, saying it stands ready as the Asean chair to facilitate discussions on how the bloc can best pursue peace in Myanmar.

data.title: Bangkok’s iconic buses to live on after surviving floods
data.description: Bangkok’s iconic cream-red buses will live on, with selected vehicles to be repurposed for emergency reserves after the ageing fleet proved its worth transporting passengers during the 2026 flood, says the director of the Bangkok Mass Transit Authority (BMTA).

data.title: Tigray rebels abandon regional capital in Ethiopia
data.description: ADDIS ABABA - Tigray rebels were abandoning their regional capital in northern Ethiopia on Saturday, a local journalist and residents told AFP, as pro-government forces advanced on the city.

data.title: New land formations linked to Anak Krakatau eruptions
data.description: JAKARTA - ⁠Anak ⁠Krakatau volcano in Indonesia expanded by ​81 acres (33 hectares) after recent eruptions produced lava flows, while ​satellite imagery detected two ‌new land formations nearby, the country’s Geology Agency said.

data.title: AWC Turns to Attractions to Lift Yields Ahead of REIT Injections
data.description: AWC unveils plans for an urban DreamWorks water park at Asiatique as part of a multi-billion-baht lifestyle expansion in Bangkok

data.title: Ageing well: Staying mobile is key to long-term health
data.description: As people grow older, changes can occur throughout the body, including in the bones, muscles and joints. Joint degeneration and a gradual reduction in mobility can affect a person’s ability to carry out everyday activities.

data.title: Phuket delivery rider held for B3.7m in house thefts
data.description: PHUKET - A food delivery rider has been arrested on charges of breaking into two homes belonging to foreigners on this tourist island and making off with valuables, including cash and camera equipment, worth nearly 3.7 million baht.

data.title: Crusader for crime victims faces money-laundering charges
data.description: Cybercrime police arrested crime victims’ rights activist Atchariya Ruengrattanapong outside a boxing stadium in Samut Sakhon on Saturday on charges including money laundering.

data.title: ONE Championship: Dzhamil Osmanov dismantles Ben Woolliss to earn US$100,000 contract
data.description: Dzhamil Osmanov dismantled Ben Woolliss with three knockdowns in 84 seconds to earn a US$100,000 ONE Championship contract and join older brother Elbrus on the promotion’s main roster.

data.title: ONE Championship: Eersel, Jarvis reunite in hospital after ‘fight of the year’ thriller
data.description: Regian Eersel and George Jarvis both ended up in hospital after a brutal ONE Championship title fight, with the champion revealing a broken right arm and the English challenger saying he had fractured his eye socket.

data.title: North Korea fires missile after Seoul’s apology demand
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea fired a ballistic missile, Seoul’s military said on Saturday, days after demanding an apology for a blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the DMZ that it blames on the North.

data.title: Two Japanese rescued after being forced into border scam work
data.description: Thai police have rescued two Japanese men who said they were forced to travel to Thailand to work for a scam gang across the border in Myanmar, where they were made to defraud elderly people in Japan.

data.title: US regulator: Boeing 737 Max software bug ‘not a safety concern’
data.description: NEW YORK - A software bug that delayed the US certification of Boeing’s 737 Max 10 aircraft does not pose a safety concern, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said on Friday after an investigation.

data.title: Fresh protests to hit Spain after housing reforms defeated
data.description: MADRID - Fresh protests over housing are due to take place in Madrid and other Spanish cities on Saturday, a day after parliament rejected two government measures to strengthen protection for tenants.
